message.content:
**Hydrogen (H)** – the simplest and most abundant element in the universe – has a wide range of physical, chemical, and nuclear properties that make it unique among the elements. Below is a concise overview of its key characteristics:

| Category | Property | Value / Description |
|----------|----------|---------------------|
| **Basic Atomic Data** | Symbol | H |
| | Atomic number | 1 |
| | Atomic mass (average) | 1.008 u |
| | Electron configuration | 1s¹ |
| | Isotopes | Protium (¹H, 99.98 %), Deuterium (²H, 0.02 %), Tritium (³H, trace) |
| | Electronegativity (Pauling) | 2.20 |
| | First ionization energy | 13.598 eV (1312 kJ mol⁻¹) |
| | Electron affinity | –72.8 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| **Physical Properties (at STP)** | State | Gas |
| | Color | Colorless |
| | Odor | Odorless |
| | Taste | Tasteless |
| | Density | 0.08988 g L⁻¹ (≈0.0000899 g cm⁻³) |
| | Boiling point | –252.87 °C (20.28 K) |
| | Melting point | –259.16 °C (14.01 K) |
| | Specific heat (gas) | 28.836 J mol⁻¹ K⁻¹ |
| | Molar volume | 22.414 L mol⁻¹ |
| | Diffusion coefficient (air) | ~0.1 cm² s⁻¹ (fastest of all gases) |
| | Solubility in water | 1.6 × 10⁻³ mol L⁻¹ at 25 °C |
| **Chemical Properties** | Bond type | Diatomic (H₂) |
| | Bond dissociation energy | 436 kJ mol⁻¹ |
| | Flammability | Extremely flammable; explosive limits 4–75 % (v/v) in air |
| | Reactivity with oxygen | Forms H₂O (combustion) |
| | Reactivity with halogens | Forms HX (e.g., HF, HCl) |
| | Acidic behavior | Acts as a weak acid in aqueous solution (pKa ≈ 35) |
| | Basic behavior | Forms hydride ions (H⁻) in metal hydrides |
| | Oxidation states | +1 (most common), –1 (hydride), 0 (molecular) |
| | Hydrogen bonding | Strong H‑bond donor/acceptor in H₂O, NH₃, HF |
| | Role in organic chemistry | Found in alcohols, amines, carboxylic acids, etc. |
| **Nuclear Properties** | Nuclear spin | ½ (protium), 1 (deuterium), ½ (tritium) |
| | Magnetic moment | 2.792847 µ_N (protium) |
| | Half‑life (tritium) | 12.32 years |
| | Fusion potential | Deuterium–tritium fusion releases 17.6 MeV per reaction |
| **Applications & Significance** | Energy carrier | Hydrogen fuel cells, rocket propellant |
| | Industrial uses | Production of ammonia (Haber process), methanol, hydrogenation reactions |
| | Environmental impact | Clean combustion (water vapor only) |
| | Astrophysics | Primary fuel in stellar nucleosynthesis (proton‑proton chain, CNO cycle) |
| | Space science | Used in ion propulsion, cryogenic storage |

---

### Quick Takeaways

- **Lightest element**: Hydrogen’s low mass gives it the highest specific energy content per unit mass among fuels.
- **Highly reactive**: Forms a wide variety of compounds, from simple diatomic molecules to complex organic structures.
- **Key isotope**: Deuterium is used in nuclear fusion research; tritium is a radioactive tracer and a component of fusion fuel.
- **Energy relevance**: Hydrogen is central to both current industrial processes (ammonia synthesis, refining) and future clean‑energy technologies (fuel cells, fusion reactors).

Feel free to ask for deeper details on any of these properties or how they relate to a particular application!
